subject: Order form: subrogation / evidence access — follow up and redlines
messages:
From: Jamie Olsen <jamie@solanum.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@solanum.ai>
Date: 2026-12-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Order form: subrogation & evidence access questions

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for sending the draft order form last week. Our legal team has two items that need clarification before procurement can move to signature:

1) Subrogation: the MSA references subrogation rights for Redwood if a third-party suit recovers from the customer — can you confirm whether Redwood intends to rely on subrogation in IP infringement scenarios or only for insurance recovery?

2) Evidence access / proof-of-claim: the order form asks that we provide technical samples and logs on request. We need a clearer process (who receives requests, timelines, and a secure upload channel) — plus a limit on what is considered "technical samples" (e.g., we cannot provide production PII or full training datasets).

I've attached Solanum's internal claim questionnaire to show the types of data we may be asked for. Can your legal team propose redline language that narrows access and sets a notice/response SLA?

We looped procurement here for timeline constraints. We'd prefer to finish legal redlines this week.

Appreciate a quick confirmation and any proposed wording.

Best,
Jamie Olsen
Sr. Counsel — Solanum AI
--- attachment: Solanum-claim-questionnaire-v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Olsen <jamie@solanum.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-13T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form: subrogation & evidence access questions

Jamie —

Thanks for the clear note and the questionnaire, that helps. Quick summary of our position and next steps:

- Subrogation: Redwood's intent is not to expand subrogation beyond insurance recoveries; we do want the right to pursue recovery if we pay a third-party claim on behalf of customer and the customer has an indemnity obligation under the MSA. However, we can propose tighter language that limits subrogation to direct recoveries tied to indemnified IP claims and excludes routine insurance proceeds where Solanum has already obtained a recovery.

- Evidence access: we agree we should avoid any expectation that customers hand over production PII or whole datasets. Proposed approach in our redline: a narrow, technical-evidence definition (logs, isolated snippets, reproduction steps), a mutually agreed secure upload (S3 bucket with restricted access or an eDiscovery portal), and a 10-business-day initial review SLA with an escalation ladder for urgent claims.

I'm attaching Redwood's proposed redlines — legal added bracketed options for subrogation carveouts and an evidence template that preserves privilege where applicable. Kimberly, can you take the lead on refining the precise clause? Ben — can you flag any commercial implications for the sales-backed term?

If this looks broadly acceptable we can hop on a 20-min call to finalize.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Director, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
--- attachment: RDW-proposed-redlines.docx (docx)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Olsen <jamie@solanum.ai>, Procurement <procurement@solanum.ai>
Date: 2026-12-15T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form: subrogation & evidence access questions

Rachel / team —

Appreciate the draft. A few concrete edits I recommend so we converge quickly:

1) Subrogation carveout language: propose the following (option language included in the attached doc) — limit Redwood's subrogation to recoveries that are: (a) directly attributable to Redwood's payment of an indemnified IP claim; (b) net of reasonable defense costs; and (c) only to the extent the customer has not already received an insurance recovery for the same loss. That should address Solanum's concern about double recovery.

2) Evidence and privilege: add explicit language that (i) customer may redact PII and privileged materials prior to delivery, (ii) Redwood will accept scoped, reproducible snippets (not full datasets), and (iii) privileged materials will be logged and returned with an assertion of privilege rather than compelled disclosure.

3) Data handling / secure upload: require use of a designated secure intake channel (we propose a pre-provisioned S3 bucket with KMS encryption and access limited to designated claims responders) and a commitment to delete any non-essential samples after 90 days unless litigation hold is in effect.

4) Timing and escalation: 10 business days for initial triage, 5 business days for follow-up questions; urgent (court-ordered) requests trigger immediate counsel call.

Ben — commercial impact: the subrogation carveout is modest from a revenue perspective but important for customer signoffs. If procurement needs a simpler compromise we can offer a mutual subrogation waiver for claims under $25k.

I'll attach a redline with the exact clause language for Solanum to review; can we ask them to confirm whether a 90-day retention is acceptable? If yes I can prepare an inline tracked changes file for signature-ready language.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Olsen <jamie@solanum.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@solanum.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-18T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order form: subrogation & evidence access questions

Kimberly / Rachel —

Thanks for the clear options and the proposed guardrails. Solanum is comfortable with:
- Limiting subrogation as you suggested (net of defense costs and excluding duplicate insurance recoveries).
- The scoped evidence approach (snippets + reproduction steps) and the privilege carve-out approach.

Two quick asks from procurement before we confirm redlines:
1) Can you replace the specific S3 bucket language with a generic "secure intake portal or equivalent" so procurement can propose their preferred upload mechanism?
2) For the retention period, procurement wants 60 days rather than 90; they say shorter retention reduces operational exposure.

We're OK to take the final redline (with the two edits above) and schedule a 20-min call tomorrow to resolve the remaining micro-points. I'll upload a completed procurement spreadsheet to the DocuSign envelope after we align on the redline.

Attached: proposed_mop_signoff.xlsx (xls)

Best,
Jamie Olsen
Sr. Counsel — Solanum AI
